description:
We are a Singapore-based team building Earth Digital Twin, an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

We welcome teammates with experience in:

GIS, remote sensing and NASA satellite datasets

Climate science, agriculture and environmental research

Data science, statistical modeling and forecasting

UI/UX, 3D Earth visualization and storytellin

Our vision: Understand Earth. Predict Change. Make Better Decisions.
summary:
Earth Digital Twin is an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform designed to help people understand environmental change and make better decisions.

Our first use case focuses on farming resilience in Southeast Asia, starting with Vietnam's Mekong Delta.

The project brings together NASA Earth observation resources covering rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and vegetation. Its proposed analytical workflow connects historical trends, geographic patterns and future climate scenarios to identify potential environmental risks and opportunities.

Through an interactive Earth globe, timeline, place analysis and AI-assisted explanations, we aim to transform complex scientific information into accessible insights for farmers, researchers, governments and businesses.

Our approach addresses the Earth System Trend Detective challenge by making Earth-system changes easier to explore, compare and interpret. The MVP establishes the foundation for a broader digital twin connecting Earth's natural and human systems.
details:
The Challenge

Environmental data is distributed across different satellites, scientific datasets and geographic systems. Understanding how rainfall, temperature, soil conditions and vegetation interact is difficult, particularly for communities making agricultural and land-use decisions.

Our Solution

Earth Digital Twin brings environmental observations into a unified spatial and temporal experience.

Our initial focus is farming resilience in Southeast Asia, using the Mekong Delta as a reference region.

The platform is designed around four capabilities:

  1. Observe: Explore environmental variables on an interactive 3D Earth globe.
  2. Analyze: Examine historical trends, anomalies and rates of change for a selected region.
  3. Explain: Connect environmental indicators and investigate possible relationships using AI-assisted analysis.
  4. Explore the Future: Compare climate scenarios to understand potential risks and opportunities.

NASA Earth Science Foundation

Our selected scientific resources include:

  • GPM / IMERG: Precipitation and rainfall variability.
  • MODIS: Vegetation health and changes in greenness.
  • GLDAS: Soil-water conditions and land-surface processes.
  • MERRA-2: Historical atmospheric and climate conditions.
  • NASA POWER: Climate indicators and future projection scenarios.

The architecture uses common geographic locations, observation periods and variable definitions to make different datasets comparable.

Technology and Approach

Our technical approach uses React and TypeScript for the user interface, CesiumJS for 3D geospatial visualization, Node.js for application APIs, and Python for scientific data processing.

The proposed data architecture supports historical observations, geospatial layers, derived indicators, statistical analysis and evidence-linked AI explanations.

Innovation

Rather than displaying isolated satellite images or raw scientific data, Earth Digital Twin aims to connect multiple Earth systems in a single interactive environment.

Users can investigate how environmental conditions change across locations and time, examine supporting evidence and explore possible future scenarios.

Intended Impact

Our initial target users include agricultural planners, environmental researchers, government agencies and commercial organizations.

The long-term goal is to help them identify environmental risks earlier, improve planning decisions and discover opportunities for sustainable development.

MVP Scope and Limitations

The initial scope is limited to farming intelligence and selected Southeast Asian locations.

Historical observations and model projections must remain clearly distinguished. Relationships between variables are treated as hypotheses unless supported by appropriate scientific analysis.

The platform is intended as a decision-support tool, not a replacement for validated local forecasts or expert assessments.
